A.why: The carrying yoke is the one strong silhouette idea in the wave and no reference family has it; reads at once from pitch 50.
A.fix: Hang clear loads from the yoke ends, warm the body from iron-grey to dust white, add a burial note (wrap or grave-tag).

B.why: The most dust-white set, with a strong slate cap on top; but a pale wrapped strapped body risks linen and the body outline is a plain box.
B.fix: Colder stone-white plus rusted iron to escape linen, a bigger cap or slate hood, one big tool instead of thin straps.

C.why: Tidy but no single idea; pale grey box with a hat, iron-dark from the back, open yellow face kills the funerary read.
C.fix: Cover the face with a wrap or death mask, put the emblem's parts into one big tool shape, carry pale colour around the back.

D.why: Dark slate box helm on a pale heavy body reads clearly from above; the skull charm is the wave's only funerary note; best fit.
D.fix: Shape the helm as a burial niche (lintel, stone frame), whiten the body away from iron, make one tool big.

E.why: Niche-hood idea is good but renders as a grey bucket helm with slate pauldrons: iron's outline.
E.fix: Make the hood a draped cowl with an arched opening and covered face; swap slate plate pauldrons for a rust carrying pad.

F.why: Grey grilled visor, dark slate arms and broad shoulders read as iron; the one rust shoulder is the only difference.
F.fix: Lighten to dust white, turn the rust mantle into a full shroud over both shoulders and back, replace the visor with a dust wrap or death mask.

notes: Every candidate leans on pale grey bodies, so the iron risk is shared; the sets that escape it do so with one dark or wooden shape on top (A's yoke, D's slate helm, B's slate cap). Almost no candidate carries the funerary half of the brief (only D's skull charm), and tools are consistently too small to read from pitch 50. Back views of C, E and F read as iron. Fit is sound across the wave. A and D are the two to carry forward; a hybrid of A's yoke with D's niche helm would be worth a try.
